programme_detail_official.description: The Beca Universidad de Chile (BUCH) is a tuition benefit awarded by the Universidad de Chile through its Direccion de Bienestar y Desarrollo Estudiantil (DIRBDE) to 100 academically outstanding young people each year. It finances the full matricula and arancel of any undergraduate career or programme of the University. Its stated objective is to reward excellent academic performance and the economic support needs of young talent in the country. The award is aimed at students in the fourth year of Chilean secondary education who do not hold MINEDUC gratuidad or an equivalent full-tuition benefit.

new_scholarship.selection_notes: Preselection is scored out of 100 base points: related professional experience 40% (more than 85 months 40 pts; 61-84 months 35 pts; 37-60 months 30 pts; 12-36 months 25 pts); academic average 40% (4.6-5.0 gives 40 pts; 4.3-4.5 gives 30 pts; 4.0-4.2 gives 20 pts); socioeconomic factor 20% (SISBEN IV categories A1-B7 give 20 pts, C1-C18 18 pts, D1-D3 16 pts, D4-D21 14 pts; where no SISBEN IV is available, estratos 1-2 give 12 pts, estratos 3-4 10 pts, estratos 5-6 8 pts). Up to 10 non-cumulative bonus points are available for working as a public official or as academic, teaching or research staff at a recognised higher-education institution; for a master's in a Chilean-government priority area; for membership of an ethnic community recognised by the Ministry of the Interior; for being certified a victim of the armed conflict through the RUV; and for having been a beneficiary of an ICETEX credit or administered fund. A minimum of 55 base points is required. Tiebreakers in order: highest academic average, then preference for women as recorded on the identity card, then earliest completed submission.
new_scholarship.best_fit: Mid-career professionals from Latin America and the Caribbean who already hold unconditional admission to an accredited Chilean master's programme and have a strong academic record, limited means, or membership of a priority group.
new_scholarship.notes: Admission and funding are separate steps: the applicant must already hold an unconditional acceptance letter from a Chilean institution for a programme listed in Anexo 1, and pays all admission-related costs, before the scholarship can be applied for. Applications for programmes not in Anexo 1 are not considered. AGCID scholarships are incompatible with any other AGCID scholarship for study in Chile, and a spouse who holds an AGCID scholarship in the same call is also excluded. Scholars must return to their country of origin after the programme in order to apply and replicate what they have learned, which is stated as a condition of the award.
